Il s’agit de mon premier reportage pour: This is my first story for La Converse. I decided to write this article after a friend told me she was going to take part in a drag show to raise funds to help a trans couple settle in Canada. I thought it was an interesting story, so I started researching and discovered that the couple actually wanted to move to another U.S. state, not to Canada.
Plus tard, Jade s’est jointe à moi pour: Later, Jade joined me to help with the research, and we began thinking about how we could dig deeper into the subject. We asked ourselves to what extent the Canadian system was ready to receive and process asylum claims from trans refugees coming from the United States and seeking asylum in Canada. We contacted several organizations and collectives to find someone who would agree to talk to us about their experience claiming asylum in Canada, but because it is such a sensitive subject, we had no luck.
<strong>Sous le second mandat de Donald: Under Donald Trump’s second term, increasingly hostile anti-trans legislation is pushing transgender people in the United States to seek refuge elsewhere in the country or abroad. Some have filed asylum claims in Canada or intend to. However, for those arriving from the U.S. who are not American citizens, the Canadian asylum system is an obstacle in itself. Our report.
Céleste Trianon, juriste et militante tr: Céleste Trianon, a Montréal-based jurist and trans feminine activist who defends trans people’s rights, makes no secret of her concern about the current situation in the neighbouring country.
Seulement en 2025, <l1>121 projets de lo: In 2025 alone, <l1>121 anti-trans bills</l1> and <l2>12 executive orders</l2> were passed in the United States, limiting trans people’s access to basic health care, education and legal recognition, among other things. Although the total number of bills passed is lower than the number proposed, those that were adopted are serious enough to lead trans people to consider fleeing to Canada to claim asylum.
En 2024, elle a fondé Juritrans, une cli: In 2024, she founded Juritrans, a legal clinic located in the heart of Montréal’s Gay Village, to provide information to trans people who want to change their legal name or gender marker in Quebec, in Canada and, in some cases, in other countries.
Aujourd’hui, Céleste Trianon conseille a: Today, Céleste Trianon also advises trans people from the United States who want to move to Canada. “The persecution of these trans people has become so severe that they can no longer get a passport that matches their identity. In some cases, their passports have been flat-out refused. [They] are facing a certain persecution from the state,” the jurist explains.

L’avocate torontoise Yameena Ansari repr: Toronto lawyer Yameena Ansari represents <l1>Hannah Keager</l1>, a trans woman from Arizona who claimed asylum in Canada earlier this year. Hannah became frightened in the United States, especially after hearing rumours that President Donald Trump might invoke the Insurrection Act of 1807, which would lead to the imposition of martial law. Since her identity documents still showed the sex she was assigned at birth, she worried about what could happen if she were arrested by authorities and unable to produce matching ID. In April, she crossed the Canadian border, and her asylum claim was filed last month.
Au-delà des obstacles financiers, dépose: Beyond the financial barriers, filing an asylum claim can be extremely difficult for a variety of reasons. For Catherine Dauvergne, a law professor at the University of British Columbia who specializes in immigration and refugee law, Canada’s asylum system is not working as it should, despite a satisfactory legal framework.

Outre les longs délais d’attente, un aut: Besides the long wait times, another major obstacle is the Safe Third Country Agreement (STCA), which can exclude and marginalize non-American citizens who claim asylum in Canada. The agreement stipulates that the two countries recognize each other as safe nations. As a result, refugees who are not U.S. citizens cannot seek Canada’s protection if they have already entered the United States, and vice versa.
Selon elle, l’accord était déjà fragile: In her view, the agreement was already fragile before Trump’s second term, but the current political climate in the United States makes the STCA simply unworkable. “The Canadian government doesn’t need a court to tell it to withdraw from this agreement; it could do so at any time quite easily,” she says matter-of-factly.
En 2023, la Cour suprême du Canada a ren: In 2023, the Supreme Court of Canada issued a <l1>decision</l1> on the STCA in which it acknowledged that the United States may not be a safe country for all refugees. Although the Supreme Court noted that the agreement includes “safety valves” that prevent people from being sent back to the United States to be deported, detained and placed in solitary confinement, these are not practically accessible.
<strong>« La législation canadienne n’es: “Canadian law is not very clear on whether trans people in the United States are persecuted enough”
Selon Céleste Trianon, les obstacles aux: According to Céleste Trianon, the obstacles trans people currently face with the STCA mean that many apply for temporary resident visas, such as study and work permits, to come to Canada, because the process is less complicated than filing an asylum claim as a non-American citizen. In most cases, applying for temporary resident status does not require a lawyer, since the procedure is laid out step by step on the IRCC website.
Malgré les nombreuses <l1>décisions</l1>: Despite numerous <l1>rulings</l1> by the Federal Court of Canada on the STCA’s violation of refugees’ rights to liberty and security, the Canadian government has not stated whether the United States is still a safe country. Meanwhile, the Trump administration continues to enact laws and executive orders that further restrict trans people’s access to <l2>fundamental human rights</l2>.
« La situation ne va faire qu’empirer »,: “The situation will only get worse,” says Céleste Trianon. She nonetheless believes Canada is following the same path as the United States when it comes to trans rights. “We’ve seen a surge in extremism and anti-trans policies in Canada for about a year now,” she says.

« Les personnes qui n’ont pas d’avocat p: “People who don’t have a lawyer to help them and those who can’t afford to pay a lawyer don’t really have access to these kinds of safety valves. There’s inequality in access to legal aid for asylum seekers,” M<sup>s</sup> Dauvergne laments.
Demander l’asile peut également sembler: Claiming asylum can also seem easy. The claim can be made at any port of entry upon arrival, or online if the person is already in Canada. Then, the Canada Border Services Agency or IRCC officers determine whether a person is eligible to be referred to the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada for a hearing. However, as M<sup>s</sup> Dauvergne explains, people must have prepared their asylum claim from a legal standpoint before even arriving at a port of entry in Canada in order to benefit from the safety valves.
« À l’heure actuelle, la législation can: “Right now, Canadian law isn’t very clear on whether trans people in the United States are persecuted enough to be able to claim asylum in Canada,” adds M<sup>s</sup> Trianon.
Bien que M<sup>e</sup> Ansari se montre: Although M<sup>e</sup> Ansari is optimistic about M<sup>s</sup> Keager’s asylum claim, since the case has moved quickly, the challenge is whether Canada will consider that the United States is no longer a safe country for trans people.
« Ces personnes devront démontrer qu’ell: “These people will have to show that they cannot be protected by the state anywhere in the United States,” M<sup>s</sup> Dauvergne specifies. In her view, if Canada concludes that the United States is not a safe country for trans people, that decision could have an influence. However, it will not directly affect trans people of other nationalities who come from the United States to Canada to claim asylum under the STCA.
« C’est pourquoi nous devons nous débarr: “That’s why we need to get rid of [the STCA], because even if we have decisions establishing that trans people aren’t safe in the United States, the Safe Third Country Agreement says that if you’re claiming asylum, you have to do it in the United States first,” M<sup>s</sup> Dauvergne continues.
La juriste considère que de nombreux cha: The legal expert considers many recent legislative changes to be concerning, such as the <l1>recent Quebec policy</l1> stipulating that trans inmates will be incarcerated according to their anatomical sex. “We need a society that truly respects human dignity, which unfortunately seems to have completely disappeared over the last 10 years pretty much everywhere in Canada,” says M<sup>s</sup> Trianon.
